title: String, char[], and char*: choosing text storage

spans.text: Arduino `String` is convenient for mutable text. `char[]` is a fixed-size buffer; `char*` is a pointer and does not allocate storage by itself. Use `const char*` for string literals because they must not be modified. C strings end with `\0`; buffer size and bounds matter.

spans.title: Important note
spans.text: Repeated dynamic `String` concatenation can fragment heap on low-RAM AVR boards such as UNO; fixed buffers and `snprintf` may be better. ESP32 has more RAM, but allocation, lifetime, and bounds risks remain.
